productSummary: LocalDocu is privacy-first, local-first document automation for PDF and Word files. You select files on your device; merge, split, extract, delete pages, rotate, reorder, compress, rename, and convert run in the browser. Document contents are not uploaded for processing in the current release.

steps.name: Select files
steps.text: Choose PDF, DOC, or DOCX with Select files (multi-select). Folder pick is available when the browser supports it (best on desktop Chrome/Edge). Files stay in your browser session.

steps.name: Choose an operation
steps.text: Merge, split, extract pages, delete pages, rotate, reorder, compress, convert Word to PDF, or manage files locally.

steps.name: Run on your device
steps.text: Processing happens locally in your browser. Save with a native picker when available, or download the result — nothing is sent to a LocalDocu server for document processing.

whyLocal.title: Why local processing can matter
points: Unnecessary file transfers can be avoided for suitable workloads.
Suitable document operations can use the computing capacity you already have on your device.
You can process documents without maintaining a remote processing session.
A future desktop app can provide more resources for larger workloads and host LocalDocu AI.

faq.subtitle: Common questions about LocalDocu, privacy, supported files, offline use, mobile browsers, and LocalDocu AI.

whatIsLocaldocu.question: What is LocalDocu?
whatIsLocaldocu.answer: LocalDocu is an open-source, local-first document workspace for working with PDFs and Word documents. Supported document operations run locally in your browser rather than requiring document upload to a LocalDocu server.

areFilesUploaded.question: Does LocalDocu upload my documents?
areFilesUploaded.answer: Document processing in the current release is local. Your selected document bytes are processed on your device and are not uploaded to LocalDocu for document processing.

worksOffline.question: Can I use LocalDocu offline?
worksOffline.answer: Yes, for supported local workflows once the application has been loaded and cached by the browser. Availability of individual browser capabilities can vary by browser and device.

supportedFormats.question: What file formats does LocalDocu support?
supportedFormats.answer: LocalDocu supports PDF for merge, split, extract, delete pages, rotate, reorder, and compress. It also supports practical DOCX merge, text preview, and capacity-gated DOC/DOCX to PDF conversion (text-oriented PDF). Complex Word layouts may not be preserved exactly.

accountRequired.question: Do I need an account?
accountRequired.answer: No account is required for the current application.

howToMergePdfs.question: How do I merge PDFs privately?
howToMergePdfs.answer: Open the Merge PDF page (or the homepage workspace), select or drop two or more PDF files, arrange the order in the list, choose Merge, then save or download the result locally. Files are not uploaded for merging.

filesAfterFinish.question: What happens to my files after I finish?
filesAfterFinish.answer: Document bytes stay in your browser session and local file handles for the work you are doing. LocalDocu does not keep a cloud copy of your documents. Closing the tab or clearing site data ends the in-memory session; files you saved or downloaded remain where you stored them on your device.

reduceCloudProcessing.question: Can LocalDocu reduce unnecessary cloud processing?
reduceCloudProcessing.answer: For suitable document workflows, LocalDocu lets your own device perform processing instead of sending document data to a remote document-processing service. This can reduce unnecessary data transfer and some server-side processing for those workloads. It does not claim universal energy savings versus every cloud setup.

isOpenSource.question: Is LocalDocu open source?
isOpenSource.answer: Yes. The project is developed in the open under the Apache-2.0 license. Source code, contribution guidance, and roadmap are available through GitHub.

howToContribute.question: How can I contribute?
howToContribute.answer: You can help with code, tests, documentation, accessibility, design, and issue reports. See the Contribute page for the contributor journey and link to the GitHub repository.

mobileBrowsers.question: Does LocalDocu work on phones and tablets?
mobileBrowsers.answer: Yes for core workflows: select files (multi-select), merge, compress, convert, and download results in mobile Chrome or Safari. Folder pick, native Save As, and create-folder work best on desktop Chrome or Edge. On some phones the in-page PDF preview may be blank — open preview in a new tab. Very large files may hit browser memory limits. See the Browser & device support page for the full matrix.

heavyOperations.question: What happens when a browser cannot perform a heavy operation?
heavyOperations.answer: Some advanced or resource-intensive capabilities may exceed what a given browser or device can handle comfortably. Those workloads may be better suited to a future desktop application with stronger local resources. The web app remains focused on suitable browser workloads.

whatIsLocaldocuAi.question: What is LocalDocu AI?
whatIsLocaldocuAi.answer: LocalDocu AI is in active development for the LocalDocu desktop app. It uses an open-weight, local-device-friendly model to understand your intent and LocalDocu’s document-management capabilities, then runs complex tasks through those local engines. It is designed to work from document metadata and your request — not by sending document contents to the cloud. LocalDocu AI is Off in the current web release. We aim to release soon and welcome contributions from the open community.

discoverability.privacyBody: Document contents are processed on this device. Document files are not uploaded to LocalDocu for processing. The current release has no authentication, no document-upload backend, and no LocalDocu AI pipeline. Status indicators show local processing, cloud processing off, and LocalDocu AI off.

mergePdf.intro: Use LocalDocu to combine multiple PDF files on your device. Select the files above, reorder them in the list, then merge and save the result locally.

faq.question: Can I merge PDF files without uploading them?
faq.answer: Yes. LocalDocu merges PDFs inside your browser using JavaScript and WebAssembly. The files are read from your device, combined in memory and saved back to your device — they are never sent to a LocalDocu server.

faq.question: Is there a limit on how many PDFs I can merge?
faq.answer: There is no fixed file-count limit or daily quota. The practical ceiling is your device’s memory: a laptop handles hundreds of pages comfortably, while very large batches on a phone can run out of memory.

faq.question: How do I change the order of the merged pages?
faq.answer: Files are merged in list order. Reorder the list before choosing Merge. To rearrange individual pages afterwards, open the merged file in Reorder pages.

faq.question: Can I merge password-protected PDFs?
faq.answer: Not yet. Encrypted PDFs are rejected so nothing is silently damaged. Remove the password in a tool you trust first, then merge.

faq.question: Does the merged PDF get a watermark?
faq.answer: No. LocalDocu is free and open source and never adds watermarks, sign-up walls or daily limits.

howTo: Select or drop two or more PDF files on this page.
Reorder the list so files appear in the order you want.
Choose Merge and save or download the merged PDF on your device.
privacy: Document bytes are processed in your browser — not uploaded to LocalDocu for merging.
After the app shell is cached, supported merge workflows can continue offline.
Browser capabilities (folder picker, save dialogs) vary by browser and device.
mergePdf.note: On phones and tablets, use Select files (multi-select) and expect results to download. Folder pick and native Save As work best on desktop Chrome or Edge.

mergeDocx.intro: LocalDocu supports practical DOCX merge for suitable Word documents. Select same-type Word files above, set the order, then merge locally.
howTo: Select or drop two or more DOCX files on this page.
Arrange them in the order they should appear.
Choose Merge and save the combined DOCX on your device.

faq.question: Can I combine Word documents without Microsoft Word?
faq.answer: Yes. LocalDocu merges DOCX files in your browser, so you do not need Word installed and nothing is uploaded.

faq.question: Will formatting be preserved when merging DOCX files?
faq.answer: Text, headings and common formatting usually carry over. Complex layouts — section-specific headers, unusual styles, embedded objects — may not survive exactly, so check the result before sharing it.

faq.question: Can I merge DOCX and PDF files together?
faq.answer: Not in one step. Merge expects files of the same type. Convert the Word files to PDF first, then use Merge PDF.

faq.question: Does merging Word files work on a phone?
faq.answer: Yes for typical documents in mobile Chrome or Safari. Very large files can hit the phone’s memory limits.

behavior: DOCX files can be merged in a practical, content-oriented way.
Processing happens on your device in the browser.
Output is saved or downloaded locally — no document upload to LocalDocu.
limits: Not every Word feature or complex layout is guaranteed to survive merge.
Merge expects same-type documents (for example DOCX with DOCX).
Very large or unusual documents may hit browser capacity limits.

compressPdf.intro: Reduce PDF file size on your device. Select a PDF above, choose Balanced (keep selectable text) or Maximum (stronger shrink), pick a quality target, then compress and save locally.
howTo: Select or drop a PDF on this page.
Choose Balanced to keep text selectable, or Maximum for the smallest file.
Pick a quality target, run Compress and save the smaller PDF on your device.

faq.question: How do I compress a PDF without uploading it?
faq.answer: Open Compress PDF in LocalDocu, select the file and run Compress. Compression happens inside your browser, so the document never leaves your device — useful for contracts, payslips, medical or ID documents.

faq.question: What is the difference between Balanced and Maximum?
faq.answer: Balanced optimises images and structure while keeping text selectable and searchable. Maximum re-renders pages as images for a much smaller file, but text is no longer selectable.

faq.question: How small will my PDF get?
faq.answer: It depends on the content. Scanned and image-heavy PDFs shrink the most; text-only PDFs are often already small. LocalDocu shows the before and after size so you can try another quality target.

faq.question: Is there a file size limit?
faq.answer: In the browser, compression is limited to PDFs up to 40 MB per file to stay within device memory. Phones may need smaller files; Balanced mode uses less memory than Maximum.

faq.question: Can I compress a PDF to send by email?
faq.answer: Yes. Most email services cap attachments at around 20–25 MB. Start with Balanced; if the file is still too large, use Maximum with a lower quality target.

modes: Balanced — keeps text selectable where possible while reducing size.
Maximum — re-encodes pages as images for stronger size reduction.
Quality targets trade file size against visual fidelity.
privacy: Compression runs entirely in your browser — nothing is uploaded to LocalDocu.
After the app shell is cached, supported compress workflows can continue offline.
compressPdf.note: On phones, prefer Balanced compression and smaller PDFs. Maximum mode needs more memory. Results download when native Save As is unavailable.

pdfTools.intro: This page includes LocalDocu’s PDF operations. Each runs locally in your browser for suitable workloads — use the panels above to select files and run an operation.

faq.question: Are these PDF tools really free?
faq.answer: Yes. LocalDocu is open source under Apache-2.0. There is no account, no paywall, no watermark and no daily task limit, because processing runs on your own device rather than on paid servers.

faq.question: Do the PDF tools work offline?
faq.answer: Yes. After your first visit the app is cached by the browser, and merge, split, extract, delete, rotate, reorder and compress keep working without an internet connection.

faq.question: Which PDF features are not available yet?
faq.answer: LocalDocu does not yet do OCR, e-signatures, PDF text editing, PDF-to-Word conversion or password removal. Those are on the roadmap; the current tools focus on organising, compressing and converting.

faq.question: Which browsers are supported?
faq.answer: Current Chrome, Edge, Firefox and Safari on desktop, Android and iOS. Desktop Chrome and Edge add folder access and native Save As; see Browser & device support for details.

ops: Merge — combine multiple PDFs in list order
Compress — reduce size with balanced or maximum modes
pdfTools.outro: Select a PDF (or several for merge), choose the operation, then run and save locally. Each operation also has its own dedicated page.

docxToPdf.intro: Convert DOC or DOCX files to a readable PDF generated on your device. Select a Word file above, convert, and save locally.
docxToPdf.howToHeading: How to convert Word to PDF
howTo: Select or drop a DOC or DOCX file on this page.
Choose Convert to PDF.
Review the PDF and save it on your device.

faq.question: Can I convert Word to PDF without uploading the file?
faq.answer: Yes. LocalDocu reads the DOC or DOCX file in your browser and generates the PDF on your device. The document is not uploaded anywhere.

faq.question: Will the PDF look exactly like my Word document?
faq.answer: Not always. Browser conversion is text-oriented: text, headings and paragraphs come through, but complex layouts, columns, text boxes and some images may not match Word exactly. For pixel-perfect output, export to PDF from Word itself.

faq.question: Does it support old .doc files?
faq.answer: Yes, DOC and DOCX are both accepted. Older .doc files with unusual formatting are more likely to lose layout details.

faq.question: Why is conversion blocked for my file?
faq.answer: Conversion is capacity-gated so the browser does not run out of memory. Phones have stricter limits than desktops; try a smaller file or a desktop browser.

limits: Conversion is text-oriented and capacity-gated for browser workloads.
Complex Word layouts may not be preserved exactly.
Very large or heavily formatted documents may need a future desktop app.
docxToPdf.noteFidelity: LocalDocu does not claim full Word layout fidelity for browser conversion.
docxToPdf.notePhones: Phones enforce stricter size ceilings. If conversion is blocked, try a smaller file or wait for the desktop app for heavier jobs.

splitPdf.intro: Split a PDF into separate files, one per page, directly in your browser. Nothing is uploaded to LocalDocu.

faq.question: How do I split a PDF into separate pages for free?
faq.answer: Open Split PDF, select the file and choose Split. LocalDocu creates one PDF per page on your device — free, with no account and no upload.

faq.question: Can I split a PDF by page range instead of every page?
faq.answer: Use Extract pages for that: enter a range such as 1-3,7 to save just those pages as a new PDF. Run it once per range you need.

faq.question: Is splitting a PDF in the browser safe for confidential files?
faq.answer: Yes. The file is processed in your browser’s memory and the results are saved to your device. No copy is sent to or stored on a server.

faq.question: Does splitting reduce quality?
faq.answer: No. Pages are copied as they are — text, images and vector graphics are not re-compressed.

howTo: Select or drop a PDF on this page.
Choose Split to create one PDF for each page.
Save or download the resulting files on your device.

extractPages.intro: Keep only the pages you need. Extract selected pages from a PDF into a new file, processed locally on your device.

faq.question: How do I write the page selection?
faq.answer: Use page numbers and ranges separated by commas, for example 1-3,5,8-10. Pages are counted from 1.

faq.question: Does extracting pages change the original PDF?
faq.answer: No. LocalDocu creates a new PDF with the selected pages; the original file on your device is untouched.

faq.question: What is the difference between Extract and Split?
faq.answer: Extract saves the pages you choose as one new PDF. Split saves every page as its own PDF.

faq.question: Can I extract pages on my phone?
faq.answer: Yes. Extract works in mobile Chrome and Safari; the new file downloads to your device.

howTo: Select or drop a PDF on this page.
Enter the page numbers or ranges you want to keep.
Run Extract and save the new PDF locally.

deletePages.intro: Remove blank, duplicate, or unwanted pages from a PDF without uploading it anywhere.

faq.question: How do I remove pages from a PDF without Acrobat?
faq.answer: Open Delete pages in LocalDocu, select the PDF, enter the pages to remove (for example 2,4-6) and run it. It is free and runs in your browser.

faq.question: Can I undo deleting pages?
faq.answer: Your original file is never modified — LocalDocu saves the edited copy as a new file. Keep the original if you might need the pages again.

faq.question: Can I delete pages from a scanned PDF?
faq.answer: Yes. Page removal works the same for scanned and digital PDFs because whole pages are removed, not text.

faq.question: Is there a page limit?
faq.answer: No fixed limit. Very large documents depend on your device’s memory, especially on phones.

howTo: Select or drop a PDF on this page.
Enter the page numbers or ranges you want to remove.
Run Delete pages and save the edited PDF locally.

rotatePdf.intro: Fix sideways or upside-down pages. Rotate some or all pages of a PDF by 90°, 180°, or 270° on your device.

faq.question: Can I rotate only some pages of a PDF?
faq.answer: Yes. Enter the pages to rotate, such as 1,3-4. Leave the field empty to rotate every page.

faq.question: Is the rotation saved permanently?
faq.answer: Yes. LocalDocu saves a new PDF with the rotation applied, so it opens correctly in any PDF viewer.

faq.question: Does rotating a PDF reduce quality?
faq.answer: No. Rotation changes the page orientation only; text and images are not re-compressed.

faq.question: Can I rotate a PDF on iPhone or Android?
faq.answer: Yes. Rotate works in mobile Safari and Chrome without installing an app, and the rotated file downloads to your device.

howTo: Select or drop a PDF on this page.
Choose the pages and the rotation angle.
Run Rotate and save the rotated PDF locally.

reorderPages.intro: Put the pages of a PDF in exactly the order you want, processed entirely in your browser.

faq.question: How do I enter the new page order?
faq.answer: Type every page number once, separated by commas, in the order you want. For a 4-page file, 4,1,2,3 moves the last page to the front.

faq.question: Can I reverse the page order of a PDF?
faq.answer: Yes. Enter the pages from last to first, for example 5,4,3,2,1.

faq.question: Can I combine reordering with deleting pages?
faq.answer: Run Delete pages first, then Reorder the result. Each step saves a new file on your device.

faq.question: Are my files uploaded to reorder them?
faq.answer: No. Reordering happens in your browser; the PDF never leaves your device.

howTo: Select or drop a PDF on this page.
Enter the full new page order, for example 3,1,2.
Run Reorder and save the result locally.
reorderPages.note: List every page number exactly once, separated by commas.

offline.intro: After a production visit caches the application shell, LocalDocu can load without a network for supported local workflows.
works: App shell (HTML, JS, CSS, icons) via the service worker
Local PDF and Word operations that do not need the network
Informational pages that are part of the cached client app
refresh: A normal reload can still open LocalDocu from the service worker cache after the first visit
Hard refresh (Shift+Reload / Ctrl+Shift+R) bypasses the service worker and usually fails while offline
Refreshing always clears in-memory documents and in-progress work in this browser session
vary: First visit still needs a network to download and cache the app
Folder access, save pickers, and other browser APIs differ by browser and device
On Android Chrome, Add to Home Screen / install usually works after the first visit
On iOS Safari, use Share → Add to Home Screen; service worker offline has tighter limits than Android
Updates to the app require a connection when a new version is published
offline.outro: Offline is a product capability, not an error. Trust indicators show offline status without treating it as failure. Mobile browsers are best for select-files → run → download; full folder and native Save As remain strongest on desktop Chrome or Edge.

staysLocal: Operation execution in the browser session
privacy.doesNotHeading: What the current application does not do
doesNot: Cloud processing: Off · LocalDocu AI: Off
dataFlow: You select files on your device
LocalDocu reads them in the browser
A local document engine runs the operation
Output is saved or downloaded on your device
later: LocalDocu desktop app for heavier local workloads
LocalDocu AI in the desktop app: open-weight on-device model that uses document metadata and user intent to drive LocalDocu document-management commands (document contents stay on device)
Optional telemetry only if clearly disclosed — Phase 1 has no product analytics pipeline
privacy.note: We do not claim “100% private,” “completely secure,” or “zero data collection” as absolute guarantees. Claims match the current implementation.

howItWorks.intro: LocalDocu is a local-first workspace: you select documents on your device, choose an operation, and run it in the browser. Results are saved or downloaded locally — depending on what your browser supports.
devices: Phones & tablets: Select files → run → download. Core merge, compress, and convert work within memory limits.
Desktop Chrome / Edge: Fullest experience — folder pick, native Save As, create folder.
Other desktop browsers: Core tools via file pick + download; folder/Save As often limited.
howItWorks.framing: Preferred framing: use the computing capacity you already have. Suitable document operations can run locally instead of requiring document uploads and remote processing. Local processing can reduce unnecessary data transfer and remote compute for workloads your device can handle — without claiming universal energy efficiency.

browserSupport.intro: LocalDocu runs in your browser. What you can do depends on device APIs (file pickers, save dialogs) and memory — not on uploading documents. Processing stays on your device in the current release.
positioning: Phones & tablets (Android Chrome, iOS Safari): select files → run tool → download
Desktop Chrome / Edge: fullest web experience (folder pick, native Save As, create folder)
Desktop Firefox / Safari: core tools via file pick + download; folder / Save As limited
Desktop app (WIP): heavier workloads + LocalDocu AI — community contributions welcome
rows: May be blank — open new tab
browserSupport.footnote: *Within browser memory and capacity gates. Prefer Balanced compress and smaller files on phones. iOS Chrome uses WebKit — treat it like Safari.
mobile: Open a tool page or the homepage workspace
Tap Select files and choose one or more documents (multi-select)
Download the result — native Save As is not available on mobile web
browserSupport.note: If in-page PDF preview is blank on iOS, use Open preview in new tab. Folder pick and create-folder remain desktop Chromium strengths. UI locales ship for English, Hindi, Spanish, Portuguese, German, French, Japanese, and Simplified Chinese; Arabic/RTL layout is planned for a later release.

openSource.intro: LocalDocu is developed in the open under the Apache-2.0 license. Source code, issues, and roadmap live on GitHub. Community contributions are welcome.
openMeans: Welcome help on accessibility, documentation, testing, and design
openSource.note: The project is community-driven and developed in the open. It is not described as “community-owned” unless governance formally supports that claim.

contribute.intro: Help build LocalDocu with code, tests, documentation, accessibility improvements, design, and carefully written issues.
journey: Read the README and privacy model so local-first constraints stay clear.
Browse open issues or propose a focused improvement.
Follow CONTRIBUTING guidance for setup, branches, and pull requests.
When changing UI copy, update English catalogs under apps/web/src/i18n/locales/en/ (other locales fall back until translated).
Keep document processing local — do not introduce upload backends or auth unless the project explicitly asks for that work.

roadmap.intro: The web workspace is the product today: local PDF and Word tools in the browser. We are actively building a LocalDocu desktop app and LocalDocu AI for intent-driven workflows on device — work in progress, aiming to release soon with the open community.
shipped: PDF merge, split, extract, delete, rotate, reorder, compress
Practical DOCX merge and text-oriented DOC/DOCX → PDF
Organize: sort, filter, rename, copy, move, folder, export
PWA app shell, themes, privacy and network status
UI locales: English, Hindi, Spanish, Portuguese, German, French, Japanese, Simplified Chinese
next: Desktop app for heavier local workloads (WIP — community contributions welcome)
LocalDocu AI (desktop): open-weight on-device model → metadata + intent → LocalDocu document-management commands (in progress)
Continued hardening of tests, accessibility, and discoverability

desktop.intro: We are actively building a LocalDocu desktop application for advanced local document automation — especially workloads that exceed comfortable browser limits — and as the home for LocalDocu AI. This is work in progress (WIP). We would love to release it soon with contributions from the open community.
direction: Stronger local resources for large or complex jobs
Same local-first privacy principles as the web app
LocalDocu AI: intent understanding that drives LocalDocu document-management capabilities using document metadata
Windows-first targets under consideration in the product roadmap
desktop.note: Use the web workspace today while we build toward launch. Desktop-only features and LocalDocu AI are not in the current browser release yet — community contributions are welcome.

localAi.intro: LocalDocu AI is in active development for the desktop app: an open-weight, local-device-friendly model that understands user intent and LocalDocu’s document-management capabilities, then runs complex multi-step work through those local engines. LocalDocu AI is Off in the current web release. We aim to release soon and welcome contributions from the open community.
localAi.designedHeading: What LocalDocu AI is designed to do
designed: Run from the LocalDocu desktop application (not as a cloud AI document pipeline)
Use document metadata and your request — not document contents — to plan work
Drive LocalDocu’s existing document-management and PDF/Word operations for complex tasks
Use an open-weight model suited to capable local devices, chosen to preserve quality and performance rather than trade them away
model: You describe what you want in plain language in the desktop app
LocalDocu AI interprets intent using LocalDocu capability knowledge plus document metadata (names, types, counts, structure signals — not file contents)
A validated command plan is produced against the LocalDocu command registry
Deterministic local engines execute the plan on your device
localAi.note: LocalDocu AI is work in progress and not active in the web workspace yet. Document contents are not sent to a remote AI for processing in the current release. Join us on GitHub if you want to help ship it.

guides.intro: Short, practical guides for working with PDFs without handing them to a server — and honest comparisons with the most popular online PDF tools, so you can choose what fits your documents.

guideMergePdfWithoutUploading.intro: Most “merge PDF” websites upload your files to their servers, combine them there and send the result back. That is fine for a recipe, but not for a signed contract, a bank statement or a medical report. Here are three ways to merge PDFs where the files never leave your device.

sections.heading: Quick answer
paragraphs: Open LocalDocu’s Merge PDF page, select your PDFs, put them in order and choose Merge. The merge runs inside your browser, so nothing is uploaded — and it works on Windows, Mac, Linux, Android and iPhone without installing anything.

sections.heading: Method 1: In your browser with LocalDocu (any device)
paragraphs: LocalDocu is free, has no file-count limit or watermark, and keeps working offline after your first visit. To merge:
steps: Go to localdocu.org/merge-pdf.
Select or drag in two or more PDF files.
Drag the list into the order you want the pages to appear.
Choose Merge, then save or download the combined PDF.

sections.heading: Method 2: Preview on a Mac
steps: Open the first PDF in Preview.
Choose View → Thumbnails to show the sidebar.
Drag the other PDFs into the sidebar where you want them.
Choose File → Export as PDF to save the merged file.

sections.heading: Method 3: A desktop app on Windows
paragraphs: Windows has no built-in PDF merge. Offline desktop apps such as the open-source PDFsam Basic or paid Adobe Acrobat can merge locally, but need to be installed. A browser-based local tool avoids the install entirely.

sections.heading: How to check that a website really doesn’t upload your files
list: Load the page, then switch on airplane mode or disconnect Wi-Fi. If merging still works, the processing is happening on your device.
Open your browser’s developer tools (F12) → Network tab while you merge. A local tool shows no large outgoing upload request.
Read the privacy policy: phrases like “files are deleted after 2 hours” mean files were uploaded and stored for a while.

faq.question: Is it safe to merge PDFs online?
faq.answer: It depends on where the merge happens. Server-based sites receive a copy of your files and keep it for a period set in their policy. Browser-based tools like LocalDocu merge on your device, so there is no copy on anyone else’s server.

faq.question: Can I merge PDFs without internet?
faq.answer: Yes. Use Preview on a Mac, an installed desktop app, or LocalDocu after one online visit — its app is cached by the browser and merges offline.

faq.question: Does merging change the quality of my PDFs?
faq.answer: No. Merging copies pages as they are; text stays selectable and images are not re-compressed.

links.guideUploadSafety: Is it safe to upload PDFs online?

guideCompressPdfOffline.intro: You need a PDF under an email or upload limit, but the document is confidential — or you are on a train with no signal. These methods shrink PDFs without an internet connection and without sending the file anywhere.

sections.heading: Quick answer
paragraphs: Open LocalDocu’s Compress PDF page once while online. After that it works offline: select the PDF, choose Balanced (keeps text selectable) or Maximum (smallest file), and save. The file never leaves your device.

sections.heading: Method 1: LocalDocu in the browser (Windows, Mac, Linux, Android, iPhone)
steps: Visit localdocu.org/compress-pdf once with a connection so the app is cached.
Select or drop your PDF (up to 40 MB per file in the browser).
Choose Balanced first; switch to Maximum with a lower quality target if you need it smaller.
Compare the before and after size, then save the result.

sections.heading: Method 2: Preview on a Mac
paragraphs: Open the PDF in Preview, choose File → Export, and set Quartz Filter to “Reduce File Size”. It is fast but often aggressive — images can become very blurry, so check the result.

sections.heading: Method 3: Ghostscript (command line, all platforms)
paragraphs: If you are comfortable with a terminal, the free Ghostscript tool compresses offline with presets such as /screen (smallest), /ebook (balanced) and /printer (higher quality):

sections.heading: Which PDFs compress best?
list: Scanned documents and photo-heavy PDFs usually shrink the most.
Text-only PDFs are often already small; expect modest savings.
If you must keep text searchable, avoid modes that turn pages into images (LocalDocu’s Maximum, Ghostscript’s /screen on some files).

faq.question: Can I compress a PDF without uploading it?
faq.answer: Yes. LocalDocu, Mac Preview and Ghostscript all compress on your own device. Most compression websites upload the file to their servers first.

faq.question: How do I get a PDF under 1 MB?
faq.answer: Try LocalDocu’s Maximum mode with a lower quality target. Text-heavy multi-page documents may not reach 1 MB without becoming hard to read; splitting the document is an alternative.

faq.question: Why didn’t my PDF get smaller?
faq.answer: It may already be optimised, or consist mostly of text and fonts. Compression mainly reduces images.

guideIsItSafeToUploadPdfsOnline.intro: Online PDF tools are convenient, and the big ones use encrypted connections and delete files automatically. But “uploaded and deleted later” is not the same as “never uploaded”. Here is what really happens to an uploaded PDF, which documents deserve extra care, and how to check any tool in under a minute.

sections.heading: Short answer
paragraphs: For everyday, non-sensitive files, reputable online PDF tools are generally fine. For identity documents, financial, medical, legal or client files, prefer a tool that processes the PDF on your own device so no copy ever exists on a third-party server.

sections.heading: What happens when you upload a PDF
steps: Your file is sent over an encrypted connection (HTTPS) to the provider’s servers.
It is stored there while it is processed — and usually for a retention period afterwards, commonly between one and a few hours on popular services, longer if you save it to an account.
The provider, its hosting company and any subcontractors operate under their own security practices and the laws of the countries where the servers are.
The result is sent back for you to download.
sections.note: Reputable providers protect this process well. The remaining risk is that a copy exists outside your control for a while — exposed to breaches, misconfiguration, legal requests or policy changes.

sections.heading: Documents you should think twice about uploading
list: Passports, ID cards and driving licences
Bank statements, tax returns and payslips
Medical records and insurance claims
Contracts, NDAs and anything under a confidentiality obligation
Client or patient data covered by GDPR, HIPAA or similar rules

sections.heading: A one-minute checklist for any PDF tool
list: Does it work offline? Load it, disconnect from the internet and try a task. If it works, your file is processed locally.
What does the privacy policy say about retention? “Deleted after X hours” means the file was stored.
Where are the servers, and who are the subprocessors?
Is an account required, and are files saved to it by default?
Is the code open source, so claims can be verified?

sections.heading: The local alternative
paragraphs: Browser-based local tools such as LocalDocu run the PDF engine inside your browser using WebAssembly. Merging, splitting, compressing and rotating happen on your device, the code is open source, and the app works with the network switched off — so there is nothing to delete later, because nothing was uploaded.

faq.question: Do online PDF converters keep my files?
faq.answer: Most reputable services delete uploaded files automatically after a retention window stated in their privacy policy — often one to two hours — unless you save them to an account. Local tools never receive the file at all.

faq.question: Is HTTPS enough to keep my PDF private?
faq.answer: HTTPS protects the file in transit. It does not change the fact that the provider receives and stores a copy while processing it.

faq.question: How can I tell if a PDF tool processes files locally?
faq.answer: Turn off your internet connection after the page loads and run a task. If it still works, processing happens in your browser.

guideEditPdfOnPhoneWithoutApp.intro: You do not need to install an app — or upload your files — to merge, split, rotate or compress a PDF on your phone. A modern mobile browser can do it on the device itself.

sections.heading: Quick answer
paragraphs: Open localdocu.org in Safari (iPhone/iPad) or Chrome (Android), tap the tool you need, select your PDFs from Files or Downloads, run it, and the result downloads to your phone. Nothing is uploaded.

sections.heading: On iPhone or iPad (Safari)
steps: Open localdocu.org and tap a tool such as Merge PDF.
Tap Select files and choose PDFs from the Files app (iCloud Drive, On My iPhone or Downloads).
Run the task, then tap the download to save it to Files.
Optional: Share → Add to Home Screen to use it like an app, including offline.
sections.note: If the in-page PDF preview looks blank on iOS, open the preview in a new tab — the file itself is fine.

sections.heading: On Android (Chrome)
steps: Open localdocu.org and choose a tool.
Tap Select files and pick PDFs from Downloads, Drive or another folder.
Run the task; the result is saved to Downloads.
Optional: menu → Install app (or Add to Home screen) for offline use.

sections.heading: What you can do on a phone
list: Merge PDFs and Word documents
Split a PDF, extract or delete pages
Rotate and reorder pages
Compress PDFs (Balanced mode uses less memory on phones)
Convert Word documents to PDF (smaller files work best)

sections.heading: Built-in alternatives
paragraphs: On iPhone, the Files app can combine files: select several PDFs, tap More (…) → Create PDF. Markup can rotate pages. Android has no built-in PDF merge, which is where a browser tool helps most.

faq.question: Can I merge PDFs on iPhone for free?
faq.answer: Yes — with LocalDocu in Safari, or the Files app’s Create PDF action. Neither requires uploading the files.

faq.question: Why did a large PDF fail on my phone?
faq.answer: Phones have less memory available to the browser than laptops. Try fewer or smaller files, use Balanced compression, or switch to a desktop browser for very large jobs.

faq.question: Does it work without mobile data?
faq.answer: Yes, after the first visit. Add LocalDocu to your home screen and it opens and processes files offline.

LocalDocu takes the opposite approach: the PDF engine runs in your browser, so files never leave your device. This page compares the two factually so you can pick the right tool for each document.

faq.question: Is there an iLovePDF alternative that doesn’t upload files?
faq.answer: Yes. LocalDocu runs merge, split, extract, delete, rotate, reorder and compress entirely in your browser, so files are never uploaded. It is free and open source.

faq.question: Does iLovePDF store my files?
faq.answer: According to iLovePDF’s privacy policy, uploaded files are processed on its servers and deleted automatically within two hours. Documents used with its e-signature service follow a separate, longer retention policy.

faq.question: Is LocalDocu as powerful as iLovePDF?
faq.answer: No — iLovePDF has many more tools. LocalDocu focuses on the most common organising and compression tasks and does them without uploads. Many people use LocalDocu for sensitive files and a server-based tool for jobs like OCR.

faq.answer: LocalDocu is free with no task limits or sign-up, because processing runs on your device instead of paid servers. It covers merging, splitting, page editing, compression and Word-to-PDF.

faq.question: Does Smallpdf upload my files?
faq.answer: Yes. Smallpdf processes files on its servers. Its privacy notice states that files processed with most tools are deleted after one hour, while files you store in an account are kept until you delete them.

faq.question: Can LocalDocu replace Smallpdf entirely?
faq.answer: For organising and compressing PDFs, often yes. For e-signing, OCR or editing text in a PDF, you will still need a tool like Smallpdf or Acrobat.

faq.question: What is a free alternative to Adobe Acrobat for merging PDFs?
faq.answer: LocalDocu merges PDFs free in your browser with no sign-up, watermark or upload. Mac users can also use Preview.

faq.question: Does Adobe Acrobat online upload my files?
faq.answer: Yes. Adobe states that files used with its online tools are handled by its servers and deleted unless you sign in and save them. The desktop Acrobat app processes files on your computer.

faq.question: Can LocalDocu edit text in a PDF like Acrobat?
faq.answer: No. LocalDocu works with whole pages and files — merging, splitting, rotating, reordering, compressing and converting. Text editing, OCR and e-signing are not available.
